claims.evidence: Original: "MedlinePlus places hydroxychloroquine in a group ..." | Retrieved: MedlinePlus: antimalarial class; antirheumatic drug.
claims.newSentence: MedlinePlus places hydroxychloroquine in a group of medicines called antimalarials and also describes it as an antirheumatic drug.

claims.evidence: Original: "The NHS describes hydroxychloroquine as a DMARD that calms the immune system." | Retrieved: NHS: DMARD that works by blocking effects of chemicals released when immune system attacks the body.
claims.newSentence: The NHS describes it as a disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) that works by blocking the effects of chemicals released when the immune system attacks the body.

claims.evidence: Original: "The Royal College of Ophthalmologists publishes eye-monitoring recommendations ..." | Retrieved: RCOphth publishes monitoring recommendations for hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine retinopathy.
claims.newSentence: The Royal College of Ophthalmologists publishes eye-monitoring recommendations for users of hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine.

claims.evidence: Original: "How these medicines calm the immune system has not been fully worked out. Reviews describe them building up inside lysosomes ..." | Retrieved: Reviews: accumulate in lysosomes, raise pH, inhibit antigen processing; 2024 review: mechanism not yet fully elucidated.
claims.newSentence: Reviews describe hydroxychloroquine building up in lysosomes and disrupting how immune cells process antigens, and one review notes that its exact mechanism has not been fully worked out.

claims.evidence: Original: "Retinal damage ... largely irreversible, so eye monitoring is recommended." | Retrieved: RCOphth: retinopathy largely irreversible; baseline test not recommended, monitoring recommended.
claims.newSentence: Retinal damage from these medicines is largely irreversible, so eye monitoring is recommended.

claims.evidence: Original: "The Royal College says extra risk factors can justify starting eye monitoring earlier." | Retrieved: RCOphth: additional risk factors may justify annual monitoring from the start.
claims.newSentence: The Royal College says extra risk factors can justify eye monitoring from the start of treatment, as decided by the prescriber.

claims.evidence: Original: "The prescriber, not the eye specialist, decides whether to stop treatment." | Retrieved: No retrieved source for the prescriber-not-eye-specialist decision.
Original: "(new)" | Retrieved: RCOphth: chloroquine appears more retinotoxic than hydroxychloroquine.
claims.newSentence: The Royal College says chloroquine appears to be more retinotoxic than hydroxychloroquine.

claims.evidence: Original: "The Royal College lists tamoxifen use as a factor that can justify earlier eye monitoring." | Retrieved: RCOphth: tamoxifen use is an additional risk factor.
claims.newSentence: The Royal College lists tamoxifen use as a factor that can justify eye monitoring from the start of treatment.

claims.evidence: Original: "NRAS advises contacting the GP or specialist team about any change in vision." | Retrieved: NRAS: contact GP or specialist team about any vision change.
claims.newSentence: NRAS advises contacting the GP or specialist team about any change in vision .
